rationale: Pivot from xgb_recency_consensus (15-iter sweep #676-690 plateaued at iter #688's 5/7 ann +27.2%, no monotone improvement past that point — sweep is saturating its 14-dim HP space). New xgb_day_quality_consensus default 1/7 ann +1.1% is SIGNIFICANTLY higher than recency_consensus's own claude-default of 1/7 ann -28.8% — same window count but +30pp avg_ann lift unsweep. Adds two novel HP axes (day_quality_floor, day_quality_weight) that train mode hasn't probed. Default w=1.0 / floor=0.30 over-suppresses on bear test (W7 worsened from -9.8%→-45.7%) but DOUBLES W3 ann (+21.9%→+73.9%), showing head-C signal magnitude is real. Train mode should prioritize day_quality_weight ∈ [0.25, 0.75] with day_quality_floor ∈ [0.40, 0.60] (gentler head-C influence) — that subspace is where the auxiliary head adds regularization without overwhelming the recency-based core. If no HP combo beats recency_consensus's iter #688 5/7 after 10-15 sweep iters, next claude iter should pivot back.
